claim.why_it_matters: Heading at the wrong level: 6.4 is a subsection of clause 6 (##) and a sibling of '### 6.1', but is rendered at ##, the same level as its parent.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page (II-22) prints '6.4 INTER-PROGRAM COMMUNICATION' and page-106.md carries the identical text as a heading, so the heading is not missing and its wording and number match. The only difference claimed is the markdown heading depth (## vs ###), which is markdown formatting the PDF does not encode: the printed page sets 6.3, 6.3.1, 6.3.2 and 6.4 in the same plain style, and the numbering '6.4' carries the hierarchy unambiguously. The same depth is used for 6.2 and 6.3 in the transcription (only 6.1 is ###), so the claim singles out one of several equally-leveled siblings. No content or meaning changes; this is formatting, which the brief says to reject.
